_caps_note: concurrent_builders is 1, not a compute limit: every builder draws on ONE account quota, so running two in parallel halves the time to the wall and doubles what a 429 costs. The first night lost both at once, 29 minutes in, $30.87 for a wall discovered twice.
_comment: The fleet's constitution. Repo paths are relative to workspace_root ($FLYWHEEL_WORKSPACE, or ~/Workspace) so the roster is portable and says nothing about the host. Caps derive from review capacity, not compute (ADR 0006). Readable in ten seconds, diffable in review — keep it that way.
_runner: How a builder is invoked (ADR 0010). The agent is a role, not a product — swap cmd/args for a different CLI, or set FLYWHEEL_AGENT_CMD to override everywhere including shell hooks. Args here REPLACE the built-in default rather than extending it, so a runner that omits its cost flag reports no spend and every run lands UNMEASURED — keep --output-format json, or whatever the swapped-in agent calls it.
_agents_note: Cut from 8 agents across 5 roles to 2 builders (retro 2026-08). Roster.Match had exactly one call site and only ever matched role=builder; coordinator, reviewer, operator and retro were declared and never dispatched. ADR 0001: a mechanism with zero call sites cannot improve by next month.
